title: Community-Acquired Pneumonia — Step 2 CK
narrative: Pneumonia is an acute infection of the lung parenchyma. CAP refers to cases arising outside hospital or long-term care. This chapter covers the Step-2-CK required arc: clinical features, diagnostics, and treatment — with epidemiology, complications, and prognosis as supporting context. Pathophysiology and etiology are touched lightly (Step 1 territory) but included as glossary depth.

scienceAnnotations.description: Worked CURB-65 calculation in step-cards grounds severity stratification.
Differential-diagnosis flow contrasts CAP against PE, HF, lung CA — discriminative reasoning.
Closing clinical-vignette MCQ forces application of dx + tx, not memorisation.
Pathway diagram (V/Q mismatch) pairs with verbal pathophys explanation.

widgets.body: Pneumonia is one of the highest-yield Step 2 CK topics — it appears across IM, peds, and EM blocks. Knowing CURB-65 and the outpatient-vs-inpatient-vs-ICU decision distinguishes a passing answer from a stalled one.

entries.definition: The functional tissue of the lung — alveoli and capillaries where gas exchange occurs (vs the stroma, which is structural connective tissue).
Alveoli filled with exudate instead of air — appears as opaque density on chest X-ray.
When the patient says 'eee', it sounds like 'aaa' on auscultation — a sign of consolidation.
Ventilation-perfusion mismatch — alveoli are perfused but not ventilated (or vice versa), causing hypoxemia.
Pneumonia caused by Mycoplasma, Chlamydophila, or Legionella — typically subacute, dry cough, often extrapulmonary symptoms.
Severity score: Confusion, Urea>7mmol/L, RR≥30, BP<90/60, age≥65. 0-1 outpatient, 2 admit, 3-5 ICU.

steps.label: Incidence
steps.body: ~5-6 cases per 1,000 adults per year in the US. Over 1 million hospitalisations annually.

steps.label: At-risk
steps.body: Highest incidence in <2y and >65y. Smokers, COPD, asthma, immunosuppression, recent viral URI.

steps.label: Mortality
steps.body: Outpatient <1%. Admitted 5-15%. ICU mortality varies with severity and timely abx.

steps.label: Top pathogen
steps.body: Streptococcus pneumoniae remains the most common typical pathogen across age groups.

widgets.title: Pathogens — typical vs atypical vs viral

cards.title: Bacterial typical
cards.body: Strep. pneumoniae · Haemophilus influenzae · Moraxella catarrhalis. Classic lobar pattern, productive cough, high fever.

cards.title: Bacterial atypical
cards.body: Mycoplasma · Chlamydophila · Legionella. Subacute course, dry cough, headache, GI symptoms. Walking pneumonia.

cards.title: Viral
cards.body: Influenza A/B · SARS-CoV-2 · RSV · adenovirus. Often precedes a secondary bacterial infection.

cards.title: History
cards.body: Acute onset fever, productive cough (yellow/green sputum), pleuritic chest pain, dyspnea on exertion. Recent viral URI common.

cards.title: Physical exam
cards.body: Tachypnea (RR>20), tachycardia, fever. Crackles on auscultation. Egophony, increased fremitus, dullness to percussion over consolidation.

cards.title: Vitals red flags
cards.body: RR ≥30, SBP <90, HR >120, SpO2 <90% on room air, AMS. Any one triggers admission consideration.

steps.label: Take focused respiratory history + cough/fever/dyspnea screen. Auscultate.
Obtain chest X-ray — lobar OR interstitial infiltrate confirms diagnosis.
CBC, CMP. If admitted: blood cultures, sputum gram + culture, urinary antigens.
Compute CURB-65 (or PSI) to stratify severity.
C — Confusion
steps.body: New-onset altered mental status. Often subtle in elderly.

steps.label: U — Urea
steps.body: BUN > 19 mg/dL (urea > 7 mmol/L). Marker of dehydration / severity.

widgets.title: Differential diagnosis — what else could it be

steps.label: Fever + infiltrate + productive cough → CAP most likely.
Low-grade fever + pleuritic pain + risk factors (immobility, OCP) → consider PE.
Bilateral findings + orthopnea + JVD + elevated BNP → heart failure.
Smoker, weight loss, recurrent post-obstructive PNA → lung cancer workup.
Known COPD/asthma + wheezing + minimal infiltrate → exacerbation, not CAP.
Outpatient (healthy)
steps.body: Amoxicillin OR doxycycline OR azithromycin (macrolide). 5-7 days.

steps.label: Outpatient (comorbid)
steps.body: Amoxicillin/clavulanate + macrolide, OR respiratory fluoroquinolone (levofloxacin, moxifloxacin).

steps.label: Inpatient non-ICU
steps.body: Beta-lactam (ceftriaxone) + macrolide, OR respiratory fluoroquinolone monotherapy.

steps.label: ICU
steps.body: Beta-lactam + macrolide OR + fluoroquinolone. Add anti-MRSA (vancomycin/linezolid) and/or anti-Pseudomonas (piperacillin/tazobactam) if risk factors.

cards.title: Parapneumonic effusion → empyema
cards.body: Fluid collection adjacent to pneumonia. If infected (empyema) requires drainage in addition to antibiotics.

cards.title: Lung abscess
cards.body: Cavitary lesion with air-fluid level on imaging. Anaerobic coverage often needed.

cards.title: Sepsis / septic shock
cards.body: Most common cause of CAP mortality. Recognise early via SIRS/qSOFA, treat per sepsis bundle.

cards.title: ARDS
cards.body: Bilateral infiltrates, PaO2/FiO2 < 300, requiring mechanical ventilation. ICU course.

widgets.vignette: A 68-year-old man with COPD on tiotropium presents to the ED with 3 days of productive cough, fever to 38.9°C, and pleuritic right-sided chest pain. RR 28, BP 102/64, HR 110, SpO2 92% on room air. Crackles and egophony in the right lower lung field. WBC 16,400 with left shift, BUN 22 mg/dL, creatinine 1.1. CXR shows right lower lobe consolidation. He is alert and oriented.
widgets.stem: What is the next best step in management?

options.label: A
options.text: Discharge on amoxicillin 5-day course with 48-hour follow-up.
options.explanation: Wrong — CURB-65 of 2 indicates admission. Outpatient amoxicillin alone is insufficient even setting CURB aside (COPD comorbidity).

options.label: B
options.text: Admit to ward and start IV ceftriaxone + azithromycin.
options.explanation: Correct — CURB-65 = 2 (age + BUN) supports admission. Standard inpatient non-ICU empiric therapy is beta-lactam + macrolide.

options.label: C
options.text: Admit to ICU and start broad-spectrum coverage including vancomycin + piperacillin/tazobactam.
options.explanation: Overtreatment — CURB-65 = 2, no MRSA/Pseudomonas risk factors, hemodynamically stable. Reserve broad coverage for ICU-level severity with risk factors.

options.label: D
options.text: Order CT pulmonary angiography to rule out PE first.
options.explanation: PE not consistent with clear consolidation + productive cough + fever + leukocytosis. CXR findings + clinical picture establish CAP.

options.label: E
options.text: Discharge home on respiratory fluoroquinolone (levofloxacin) with 48-hour follow-up.
options.explanation: Levofloxacin is correct outpatient option for COPD comorbidity, BUT CURB-65 = 2 mandates admission. The drug choice is right; the disposition is wrong.

widgets.attendingTip: Step 2 CK loves combining CURB-65 with comorbidity. Always compute CURB-65 explicitly — the score determines disposition, comorbidity guides drug class.

widgets.title: Prognosis — what to tell the patient

steps.label: Outpatient
steps.body: <1% 30-day mortality. Most improve in 48-72 hours of appropriate abx.

steps.label: Inpatient ward
steps.body: 5-10% in-hospital mortality. Older / comorbid trend higher.

steps.label: ICU
steps.body: 15-30% mortality, higher with shock or ARDS. Mortality drops with timely (≤1hr from suspicion) antibiotics.

steps.label: Long-term
steps.body: Cough can persist 4 weeks; fatigue often longer. Pulmonary fibrosis is rare. Reinfection risk slightly elevated for 12 months.

widgets.body: References: IDSA/ATS 2019 CAP guidelines · UpToDate 'Community-acquired pneumonia in adults' · AMBOSS CAP article · NEJM 2014;370:543-51 (Mandell, severity scoring).
